questions.explanation: Constructor ke andar pehli statement ya toh 'this()' (same class ke doosre constructor ko call karne ke liye) ya 'super()' (parent class ke constructor ke liye) hoti hai.

questions.question: Which executes first?
questions.explanation: Static Initialization Block (SIB) class loading ke waqt sabse pehle execute hota hai.

questions.question: IIB executes
questions.explanation: Instance Initialization Block (IIB) har baar object create hone par constructor se theek pehle execute hota hai.

questions.question: Execution order
questions.explanation: Java mein execution ka sahi kram yeh hai: Pehle SIB (class loading par), phir IIB (object creation par), aur ant mein Constructor.

questions.question: A Java application receives thousands of requests simultaneously. Each request builds a large string by appending multiple values. The same string object is shared by multiple threads.
questions.explanation: StringBuffer thread-safe (synchronized) hota hai, isliye multi-threaded environment mein jab multiple threads ek hi object ko share karein tab yeh best hai.

questions.question: Why is StringBuilder preferred over StringBuffer in this program?

options.b: The program is single-threaded, so synchronization overhead is unnecessary.
options.d: StringBuilder uses less memory than StringBuffer

questions.correct_answer: The program is single-threaded, so synchronization overhead is unnecessary.
questions.explanation: StringBuilder thread-safe nahi hota lekin yeh fast kaam karta hai. Single-threaded program mein synchronization ki zaroorat nahi hoti, isliye StringBuilder prefer hota hai.

questions.question: A developer accidentally loses the source code (.java files), but the compiled .class files are still available. Which statement is correct?

options.a: The code is completely lost and cannot be recovered.
options.b: A Java decompiler can generate readable Java source code from the .class files, although comments and original formatting are usually lost.
options.c: The JVM can execute bytecode directly without any source code conversion.
options.d: Only comments are preserved in .class files.

questions.correct_answer: A Java decompiler can generate readable Java source code from the .class files, although comments and original formatting are usually lost.
questions.explanation: Bytecode (.class files) se decompiler ki madad se source code wapas prapt kiya ja sakta hai, halaanki comments aur formatting gayab ho jaati hain.
